expected_before.outcome_quote: We do not find a link between ADHD and EO, although we do find a positive link between ADHD and the risk-taking subdimension of EO. Hyperactivity symptoms are positively related to EO, which is mainly driven by the subdimensions proactiveness and risk-taking. We do not find a link between attention-deficit symptoms and EO, though there is a negative link between attention-deficit and proactiveness.

changes.rationale: The newly recovered published journal contains the two selected aggregate-EO findings: a positive hyperactivity/impulsivity association and a nonsignificant joint-model inattention association. The current report explicitly states those original findings and reports agreeing results. Its overall-ADHD and EO-subdimension differences are extensions, not contrasts with an original tested claim. Under codebook rule2 this supports successful rather than shipped mixed. Journal Study2 support is marginal, not p<.05, and its bivariate inattention correlation must not be confused with the conditional structural estimate. Version provenance remains explicit; no universal result-equivalence rule was adopted.

proofs.quote:
Studying the sub-dimensions of ADHD using OLS, hyperactivity is posi-
tively related to total EO (β = .10, p < .01), and attention-deficit is not asso-
ciated  with  total  EO.  Using  PLS-SEM,  we  found  similar  results  for  these 
relationships (hyperactivity: β = .11, p < .01). In terms of the EO dimensions, 
hyperactivity is not related to innovativeness but is related to both proactive-
ness (β = .10, p < .01) and risk-taking (β = .09, p < .05). Attention-deficit is 
not related to innovativeness and risk-taking but is related to proactiveness 
(β = −.11, p < .01).

Looking at the subdimensions of ADHD, the results of our analyses are 
mostly in line with the findings of Yu et al. (2018). Similar to Yu et al., we 
found a positive association between hyperactivity and EO. This effect seems 
to be driven by a positive relationship of hyperactivity with the subdimen-
sions proactiveness and risk-taking and not by a relationship with innovative-
ness. We do not find a link between attention-deficit and total EO. However, 
we do find a negative link between attention-deficit and proactiveness.

Although  we  do  not  find  an  overall  relationship  between  ADHD  and 
EO, we provide insight into the underlying links between the two constructs. 
Furthermore, we are able to replicate the positive relationship found by Yu et 
al. (2018) between hyperactivity and EO using another data set.
